dedupe_keys.name: treepedia street level green view index maps and library mit senseable city lab

description: Treepedia, from MIT's Senseable City Lab, measures and maps vegetation along city streets by computing a Green View Index (GVI), from 0 to 100, on Google Street View panoramas, estimating the share of view obstructed by tree canopy; its website maps GVI across and between cities. The public repository provides the library and workflow so others can compute GVI: sample points every 20 metres along a street network inside a boundary shapefile, collect panorama identifiers from Google, then classify six images per point with Otsu's method and mean-shift segmentation and average them into one GVI per point, written to a shapefile. Coverage: cities mapped by the lab or by users who send results; parks are excluded because Street View does not go into them. Access: free code; imagery needs Google Street View access. Licence: BSD-style for the code. Caveats: the code targets Python 2.7, and results depend on Street View coverage and dates. Simulation uses: street canopy exposure for pedestrian heat, shade routing and greening plans. Related records: the NYC street tree census and London public realm trees.
